evals.name: refactor-py-split-god-module
evals.prompt: billing.py has grown into a grab-bag of pricing, invoice rendering and email delivery. Split it into a proper billing package with separate modules. app.py and other services import from billing directly, and the tests in tests/ must keep passing.
evals.expected_output: billing/ package (e.g. pricing.py, rendering.py, delivery.py) with billing/__init__.py re-exporting the old public names so `from billing import ...` and app.py keep working; behavior identical; the mock.patch('billing.smtp_send') coupling handled consciously.
expectations: States mode = refactor and records the contract (public names TAX_RATES, compute_total, format_invoice, invoice_json, send_invoice_email, smtp_send) before editing
Runs the existing tests before and after and reports both results
`from billing import TAX_RATES, compute_total, format_invoice, invoice_json, send_invoice_email` still works without editing app.py

Notices that tests patch `billing.smtp_send` and keeps that patch effective (e.g. delivery code looks up smtp_send via the package, or the test change is explicitly called out) instead of silently breaking the mock
No behavior changes: rounding, error message 'unknown country: XX', invoice text format all unchanged
Steps are small (create package + re-exports, move one responsibility at a time) and the report lists them

evals.name: refactor-plan-only-callback-to-async
evals.prompt: Our Node service has an internal db.query(sql, params, cb) callback API that's called from about 40 files under src/ (routes, jobs, migrations). I want to move everything to async/await. Don't touch any code yet - give me a migration plan I can review with the team.
evals.expected_output: A plan only, no edits: parallel change (promise-based core + callback adapter), batches of callers, ordering/error-semantics risks, verification per phase, rollback, and a stop for confirmation.
expectations: Makes no file edits and says so
Uses an expand-migrate-contract / parallel-change sequence: add a promise API, keep the callback form as an adapter over it, migrate callers in batches, remove the adapter last
Flags behavior risks: sequential vs concurrent execution (no blanket Promise.all), error propagation and unhandled rejections, transactions/connection scope in migrations
Includes a safety-net step (characterization or integration tests for representative callers) and verification commands between phases
Includes rollback and an explicit 'out of scope' list, and asks for confirmation before Phase 1

evals.name: rewrite-legacy-js-price-formatter
evals.prompt: priceFormat.js is unreadable legacy code. Rewrite it from scratch in modern JavaScript. Invoices and the CSV export both use fmt() and formatPrice().
evals.expected_output: Characterization tests recorded from the old implementation first (including quirks), a modern rewrite exporting the same fmt/formatPrice API, a differential comparison with counts, and quirks preserved or listed under Needs approval.
expectations: States mode = rewrite and why (user asked; small surface)
Writes characterization/golden tests by running the OLD code before writing new code

Preserves or explicitly flags the quirks: 1.005 -> '$1.00' (toFixed rounding), '12abc' -> parsed as 12, -0.001 -> '-$0.00', unknown currency code used as prefix without space ('JPY0'), EUR suffix with a space, accounting parentheses, empty option
Reports the 1e21 output ('$1e,+21') as a found bug rather than silently fixing it
Keeps the exports fmt(v, c, o) and formatPrice(v, c) with the same signatures
Reports a differential result with a denominator (N inputs, M differences)

evals.name: port-python-to-go-stats-cli
evals.prompt: Port stats.py to Go as a small CLI (reads JSON on stdin, prints JSON). The nightly report diffs its output, so the output must stay byte-identical. Fixtures with expected outputs are in fixtures/ and compare.py runs any command against them.
evals.expected_output: Idiomatic Go CLI whose stdout matches all fixtures, with explicit handling of Python-vs-Go semantic differences and a parity report (4 inputs / 0 differences, or honest 'not run').
expectations: Writes a parity contract: unit = one invocation (stdin JSON -> stdout), byte-identical output required
Floor division and modulo for negatives match Python (-7 // 4 == -2, -7 % 4 == 1)
Rounding matches Python's banker's rounding (12.5 -> 12), e.g. via math.RoundToEven
Output formatting matches json.dumps: ', ' and ': ' separators, non-ASCII escaped as \uXXXX, key order as in Python (not Go's sorted map keys), 3.0 printed as 3.0 and null for empty mean
top_words ties keep first-occurrence order like Counter.most_common; word filter matches str.isalpha on Unicode; label width counts code points not bytes
Runs compare.py (or states precisely why it could not) and reports N inputs / M differences

evals.name: port-java-to-kotlin-interop
evals.prompt: Convert User.java and UserIndex.java to Kotlin. ReportJob.java stays in Java for now and has to compile and behave exactly as before.
evals.expected_output: Kotlin User and UserIndex that keep the Java-facing API (static calls, getters, checked IOException, nullable returns, duplicate-email exception) so ReportJob.java is unchanged.
expectations: UserIndex functions remain callable as static methods from Java (object/companion with @JvmStatic, or top-level with @file:JvmName('UserIndex'))
load() is annotated @Throws(IOException::class) so ReportJob's catch (IOException) still compiles
byEmail keeps throwing IllegalStateException on duplicate emails (does not silently switch to associateBy, which keeps the last value)
findName returns String? and displayName is nullable; no !! on input-dependent values
User keeps equals/hashCode on id+email only and toString 'User#<id>' (a plain data class would change both) and getters getId/getEmail/getDisplayName
Report includes verification (compile + run ReportJob on users_ok.csv and users_dup.csv with exit codes) or states it was not run

evals.name: port-c-to-rust-ffi-zh
evals.prompt: 把 ringbuf.c 移植到 Rust。C 侧的调用方代码不能改，ringbuf.h 里的 API 和行为要保持一致，现有的 test_ringbuf.c 也要能继续跑通。
evals.expected_output: A Rust crate exposing the same C ABI (opaque handle, extern "C" functions) built as a static/dynamic library, with the C test linking against it; report in Chinese.
expectations: Report is in Chinese and names the end state (Rust implementation behind the unchanged C header, C callers untouched)
Exports extern "C" functions with no_mangle matching ringbuf.h exactly; ringbuf stays opaque (Box pointer handle); rb_free(NULL) is a no-op and rb_new(0) returns NULL
Preserves free-running u32 head/tail with wrapping arithmetic (wrapping_add/wrapping_sub) and power-of-two masking instead of panicking on overflow
No panic can cross the FFI boundary (no unwrap on inputs; null pointers checked); every unsafe block has a SAFETY comment
Flags (does not silently fix) the source edge case where next_pow2 overflows for capacity > 2^31
Builds and runs test_ringbuf.c against the Rust library, or states exactly which step was not run and why

evals.name: port-python-to-rust-stats-cli
evals.prompt: Rewrite stats.py in Rust as a standalone CLI (cargo project). Same contract: JSON on stdin, JSON on stdout, and the output has to be byte-identical to the Python version because a nightly job diffs it. Fixtures and compare.py are next to the script.
evals.expected_output: Cargo project producing output identical to Python on all fixtures, handling floor division, banker's rounding, json.dumps formatting (separators, ASCII escaping, insertion order, 3.0), Counter tie order and code-point lengths; parity report.
expectations: Writes a parity contract (end state A replacement; unit = one invocation; byte-identical stdout)
Floor division/modulo match Python for negatives (div_euclid/rem_euclid or a floor helper): bucket(-7,4) == -2, offset == 1
Rounding matches banker's rounding (round_ties_even or equivalent): 12.5 -> 12
Output matches json.dumps byte-for-byte: ', ' and ': ' separators, \uXXXX escapes for non-ASCII, insertion-ordered widths keys, 3.0 and -0.875 formatting, null for empty mean
top_words tie order equals Counter.most_common (first occurrence) and isalpha filter drops '42' and 'x-ray'; widths count code points
No unwrap/expect on input-dependent values without a stated reason; errors on bad JSON reported, not panicking silently
Runs compare.py against the built binary (or states precisely why not) and reports N inputs / M differences

evals.name: port-ts-to-go-report-cli
evals.prompt: We're moving the ops tooling from Node to Go. Port report.ts to a Go CLI with the same stdin/stdout JSON behaviour — the dashboard diffs the output so it has to match exactly. Expected outputs from the current TS build are in fixtures/, and compare.py checks any command against them.
evals.expected_output: Go CLI matching all fixtures exactly, reproducing JS semantics: integer-like keys first in object order, default string sort, Math.round half-up, UTF-16 length, no HTML escaping, number formatting.
expectations: Writes a parity contract (unit = one invocation; exact stdout match)
Reproduces JS object key order: integer-like keys ascending first, then insertion order ("2","10","zoe","al")
Reproduces Array.prototype.sort default string comparison ([-3,1.5,10,100,9]) instead of numeric sort
Reproduces Math.round semantics (half toward +infinity: -1.5 -> -1, 2.5 -> 3) and note length in UTF-16 code units ("👍👍" -> 4)
JSON output matches JSON.stringify: no HTML escaping of < > (SetEscapeHTML(false)), integral floats without .0, compact separators, empty arrays as [] not null
Runs compare.py (or states precisely why not) and reports N inputs / M differences
